market_summary: Pre-market brief as of 08:32 IST, Thursday 19 Nov 2026. Verified prior close (18 Nov): Nifty 50 25,227.95 (-159.45, -0.63%) and Sensex 82,031.81 (-500.38, -0.61%). Thirteen of 16 major sectors fell; consumer durables (-3.08%), metals (-2.46%), auto (-1.35%) and IT (-1.24%) were weak, while PSU banks (+0.59%) were a relative pocket of strength. Nifty Midcap 100 fell 1.22% and Smallcap 100 fell 0.35%. Reuters' GIFT Nifty snapshot at 07:47 IST was 25,161.5, about 0.26% below the cash close and indicative of a softer start, not a cash-market opening print. Offsetting factors: Brent was near $92.12/bbl after the prior session's decline, and 18 Nov provisional cash flows showed FII buying of ₹5,866.78 crore versus DII selling of ₹3,159.90 crore. Main risk: hawkish Fed minutes, a firm dollar and elevated US yields may keep risk appetite cautious. No account holdings were accessible in this run, so stock items are prioritized by verified catalyst materiality rather than portfolio weight. Verified facts are separated from interpretation in each item; this is not a forecast or investment advice.

global_cues.title: GIFT Nifty points to a softer start
global_cues.detail: Reuters quoted GIFT Nifty at 25,161.5 at 07:47 IST on 19 Nov, versus the Nifty 50 cash close of 25,227.95 on 18 Nov (an indicative gap of about -0.26%). Futures indications can change before the cash pre-open and are not the official opening level.

global_cues.title: Fed minutes revive the risk of further US rate increases
global_cues.detail: Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed policymakers focused on inflation risks; some considered a 50-basis-point increase if incoming inflation data were unfavorable. Reuters reported markets were pricing a near-certain 25-basis-point December hike. Higher US rates could support the dollar and Treasuries and make emerging-market assets less attractive.

global_cues.title: Wall Street finished mixed after Nvidia results and Fed minutes
global_cues.detail: On 18 Nov, the Dow fell 1.12% to 50,193.03 and the S&P 500 fell 0.24% to 7,322.53, while the Nasdaq rose 0.39% to 24,429.89. Nvidia shares fell despite better-than-expected results and guidance, underscoring uncertainty around AI valuations and leadership.

global_cues.title: Crude remained lower after a larger US inventory build
global_cues.detail: At 02:37 GMT on 19 Nov, Brent traded at $92.12/bbl and WTI at $83.17/bbl after falling 1.3% and 3.2%, respectively, in the previous session. US crude inventories rose 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million for the week ended 13 Nov, versus a Reuters poll expectation of a 58,000-barrel increase. Shipping risks in the Strait of Hormuz remain a countervailing supply risk.

global_cues.title: Japan opened modestly higher, but broader regional signals were mixed
global_cues.detail: At 00:25 GMT on 19 Nov, Japan's Nikkei was up 0.2% at 59,159.40 while the broader Topix was down 0.4% at 3,809.53. Chip and retail gains offset weakness in metals, energy and banks.
global_cues.source: The Wall Street Journal (19 Nov 2026, 00:25 GMT)

intraday.headline: InvaGen's New York facility receives USFDA 'No Action Indicated' classification
intraday.what_changed: Cipla's exchange filing says the USFDA communicated on 17 Nov that its inspection of wholly owned subsidiary InvaGen Pharmaceuticals' Hauppauge, New York facility (conducted 19-22 Oct 2026) was classified as No Action Indicated (NAI).
intraday.why_it_matters: The NAI outcome removes a near-term regulatory overhang for this specific facility and is a positive compliance signal. It does not establish the regulatory status of Cipla's other facilities or guarantee any revenue change.
intraday.risk: The outcome applies only to the inspected InvaGen site; no direct financial impact or incremental product approvals were quantified in the filing.
intraday.source: Cipla disclosure to NSE and BSE under Regulation 30 (17 Nov 2026)

intraday.headline: DRI search at Vikhroli office and Bhiwandi depot over imported-product classification
intraday.what_changed: Cipla disclosed that the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence's Mumbai zonal unit searched its Vikhroli office and Bhiwandi depot on 16 Nov under Section 105 of the Customs Act. The filing says the matter relates to classification or exemption of an imported finished pharmaceutical product; Cipla said it cooperated. The company separately stated there was no material impact on financials, operations or other activities.
intraday.why_it_matters: This is a regulatory and customs headline to monitor alongside the positive InvaGen NAI outcome. The filing does not identify the product or quantify any duty exposure, and a search by itself does not establish wrongdoing.
intraday.risk: The underlying product classification or exemption question remains unspecified; any subsequent demand, penalty or further regulatory action is unknown.
intraday.source: Cipla disclosure to NSE and BSE under Regulation 30 (16 Nov 2026)

swing.headline: Q2 FY27 press release reports strong year-on-year growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT
swing.what_changed: The 18 Nov company press release reports Q2 FY27 operating revenue of ₹125.56 crore (+28.92% YoY), EBITDA of ₹17.31 crore (+92.98%) and PAT of ₹10.54 crore (+130.63%). H1 FY27 revenue was reported at ₹232.59 crore (+35.63%) and PAT at ₹20.77 crore (+51.16%). Important disclosure nuance: the exchange-cover letter describes the results as standalone, while the press-release footnote labels the figures consolidated; confirm the basis against the detailed results before making period comparisons.
swing.why_it_matters: The reported EBITDA and PAT growth suggest improved operating leverage and stronger profitability, which may keep the result in focus. The conflicting standalone/consolidated description lowers confidence in like-for-like interpretation.
swing.risk: Newly listed small-cap with limited trading history and potential liquidity/volatility risk; result-basis discrepancy should be reconciled with the detailed financial statements. No valuation conclusion is implied.
swing.source: BLS Polymers press release filed with NSE and BSE (18 Nov 2026)

investing.headline: NALCO signs MoU with RUSAL to explore scandium recovery from red mud
investing.what_changed: NALCO's 18 Nov exchange-filed press release confirms an MoU with RUSAL for collaboration on recovery of scandium from red mud, signed on the sidelines of the 44th ICSOBA conference in Bengaluru on 17 Nov. The stated scope is knowledge exchange and evaluation of viable recovery pathways.
investing.why_it_matters: Scandium is a critical mineral used in advanced industrial and clean-energy applications; successful recovery could create longer-term value from an alumina-refining by-product and add strategic-minerals optionality. The announcement is an early-stage collaboration, not a disclosed commercial project.
investing.risk: No recovery volumes, capex, project timetable, binding offtake, commercial terms or earnings contribution were disclosed; technical and economic feasibility remain unproven.
investing.source: National Aluminium Company disclosure to NSE and BSE under Regulation 30 (18 Nov 2026)

macro.name: USD/INR and US Dollar Index — 18 Nov close
macro.context: Reuters reported the rupee ended almost unchanged after reaching a seven-month intraday high of 93.2550; a firmer dollar offset foreign-flow support. DXY was reported up 0.2% to 103.8.

macro.name: Brent and WTI crude — 19 Nov, 02:37 GMT
macro.context: Prices were little changed after declines in the previous session. The EIA reported US crude stocks up 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million for the week ended 13 Nov, substantially above the Reuters poll expectation of +58,000 barrels. Lower crude can ease India's import bill, but Gulf shipping risks remain.

macro.context: AP reported the yield eased from 5.10% late Tuesday as oil prices fell. The level remains elevated and may matter for global discount rates and emerging-market risk appetite.
